key_insight: TideCache aims to make hybrid LLM serving more memory-efficient by dynamically sharing GPU memory across different cache types and managing cache residency between GPU and host memory.
problem_solved: Hybrid language models combine global-attention layers with bounded-state layers, creating different cache requirements that change with context length and concurrent requests. Serving systems must allocate limited GPU memory efficiently across these competing demands.
method: Target CPU–GPU superchips to coordinate cache storage across GPU and host memory.
Use a Transparent Cache Pool to redistribute physical memory pages among cache components while preserving fixed virtual addresses.
Incorporate layer-wise streaming, as indicated by the title; the supplied abstract is truncated and does not describe its implementation or the remaining components.
impact: More adaptable cache management could help practitioners use GPU memory more efficiently when serving hybrid LLMs under changing workloads. The supplied excerpt does not include performance measurements.

paper_title: TideCache: Efficient Hybrid LLM Serving with Transparent Cache Management and Layer-Wise Streaming
paper_authors: Jinbin Luo, Xiaozhe Yao, Shang Yang, Zhijian Liu, Song Han
